question: According to health standards, what does reproductive health truly cover?

options.A: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being
options.B: The prevention of genetic disorders in newborns
options.C: Only the absence of sexually transmitted infections
options.D: Biological fitness solely for childbearing purposes

explanation: You got this! Reproductive health is much more than just a healthy body or the absence of disease—it embraces your total physical, mental, and social wellness. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do nurses look at reproductive health as a lifelong journey rather than just a passing phase?

options.A: Because reproductive needs change and persist from birth to old age
options.B: Because healthcare funding is tied to lifelong patient monitoring
options.C: Because reproductive organs never undergo natural degeneration
options.D: Because patients only seek care during their childbearing years

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive health matters at every single stage of life, meaning our care and guidance as nurses never truly stop. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which hormone is the main driver of male reproductive development?
explanation: Great job! Testosterone is the key male sex hormone made in the testes that shapes male physical traits and reproductive function. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of the fallopian tubes in the female body?

options.A: To serve as the usual site for fertilization of the egg
options.B: To provide a muscular environment for fetal development
options.C: To secrete large amounts of protective progesterone
options.D: To produce the monthly supply of mature oocytes

explanation: You nailed it! The fallopian tubes catch the released egg and act as the meeting place where sperm usually fertilize it before it moves to the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the medical term for a young girl's very first menstrual period?
explanation: Well done! Menarche is simply the medical word for that first major milestone of monthly bleeding during puberty. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support just as crucial as physical checks during teenage puberty?

options.A: Mental health counseling replaces the need for nutritional guidance
options.B: Rapid bodily changes often cause anxiety, confusion, and body image issues
options.C: Teenagers refuse physical examinations unless given psychological counseling
options.D: Hormonal surges permanently impair the adolescent's cognitive abilities

explanation: Exactly right! Teens go through a whirlwind of physical and emotional shifts, so offering a listening ear is a big part of good nursing care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h3)

question: As women grow older, which health screenings become most important?
explanation: Spot on! Regular checks for cervical changes and breast health are vital preventative steps as women age. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h4)

question: A 52-year-old woman comes to the clinic reporting hot flashes and irregular periods. What stage is she likely going through?
explanation: You got it! Those sudden hot flashes and wonky cycles are classic signs of perimenopause, the transition phase leading up to menopause. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a major public health challenge for reproductive health in Nigeria?

options.A: Limited access to modern contraceptive methods
options.B: Universal excess availability of fertility treatments
options.C: High maternal mortality ratios in rural areas
options.D: High burden of sexually transmitted infections

explanation: Correct! Too many fertility treatments are definitely not the problem here—rather, it's struggling with basic maternal care access and preventable complications. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h5)

question: How do poverty and cultural barriers team up to worsen pregnancy outcomes in tough settings?

options.A: They cause immediate cessation of all hormonal activities
options.B: They automatically increase the biological rate of twin pregnancies
options.C: They eliminate the need for community health nursing outreaches
options.D: They delay timely care-seeking and restrict access to skilled birth attendants

explanation: Spot on. When money is tight or cultural beliefs hold sway, women often reach the hospital too late, leading to avoidable emergencies. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the heart of reproductive rights?

options.A: The mandatory requirement for every adult to have children
options.B: Free cosmetic surgeries for all citizens reaching adulthood
options.C: Bodily autonomy and freedom from coercion in health decisions
options.D: Government control over family size and birth intervals

explanation: You nailed it! Reproductive rights mean every person has the right to make their own free choices about their body and family planning. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why do modern healthcare programs make sure to involve male partners in reproductive health?

options.A: Men are the only family members who suffer from reproductive infections
options.B: Men often influence household health decisions and resource allocation
options.C: Male involvement completely removes the need for female health education
options.D: Women are legally prohibited from visiting clinics alone

explanation: Great reasoning! Since men often hold the purse strings and make major home decisions in many communities, getting them on board is key to success. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a core day-to-day nursing duty when it comes to reproductive health care?

options.A: Passing national laws regarding reproductive rights
options.B: Performing major obstetric surgical operations independently
options.C: Providing family planning counseling and education

explanation: Exactly right! Nurses spend a lot of time guiding clients through family planning choices and teaching healthy habits. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is keeping strict privacy and confidentiality so important when teenagers come in for reproductive health services?

options.A: It removes the need to document clinical findings in health records
options.B: It is a legal requirement only for adult patients, not minors
options.C: It builds trust and encourages teens to seek necessary medical advice early
options.D: It prevents parents from ever knowing their child is growing up

explanation: You got it! Teens are often scared of being judged. Promising confidentiality helps them feel safe enough to get help before small issues turn big. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T2#GNS216_U1_T2_h7)
